item.title: Troops raid bandits’ hideout in Kogi, recover AK-47 rifles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation. The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targeted suspected kidnappers operating in the Osara, Gada and Ohakiti forest areas of Okehi Local Government Area, following intelligence reports on their activities and hideouts. In a statement, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the operation was launched by troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba in collaboration with other security personnel. She said the operation was aimed at dismantling criminal hideouts linked to the recent spate of kidnappings along the Kabba–Okene Road and neighbouring communities. According to the statement, troops encountered about six armed bandits at an abandoned settlement within the forest during the offensive, engaging them and forcing them to flee. A subsequent search of the hideout led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered from the enclave included bags, torchlights, food supplies and a power bank believed to have been used by the fleeing suspects. The Army said the operation underscored its determination to deny criminal elements freedom of action, dismantle their operational bases and restore security along vulnerable routes and communities in Kogi State. It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property. The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to identify and clear hideouts used by criminal elements across the country. item.title: Ekiti govt disowns purported climate action award
item.description: The Ekiti State Government has dissociated itself, Governor Biodun Oyebanji and his administration from a purported Best African Governor for Climate Action Award reportedly presented to the Governor. According to a publication, the award was presented by the King’s College African Leadership Centre at its inaugural Climate Action Awards ceremony, held on the sidelines of COP 31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in collaboration with the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (OSOPADEC). The Government, however, wishes to state categorically that Governor Oyebanji was neither aware of the purported award nor involved in its presentation. He did not attend the ceremony, nor authorise anyone to receive it on his behalf. This disclaimer has become necessary to set the record straight and prevent members of the public from being misled by claims that are not only false but could also be part of a dubious publicity stunt. Governor Oyebanji’s administration is guided by the principles of accountability, transparency and integrity. While the Governor has received several recognitions and awards from credible organisations and reputable institutions in acknowledgement of his contributions to governance and development, the Governor does not endorse or associate himself with questionable awards from organisations whose credibility and intentions are unclear. Members of the public and the media are therefore urged to disregard the report and treat the purported award as unauthorised and unrecognised by the Governor and the Ekiti State Government. item.title: Otti disowns viral statement against campaign rallies, calls it fake
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has disowned a viral social media statement purportedly credited to him, describing it as fake and warning the public against spreading misinformation. The statement, which circulated on X (formerly Twitter), quoted Otti as saying that incumbent governors who embark on campaigns have no business doing so if they have performed well, arguing that their achievements should speak for them and secure their re-election. It also quoted the governor as saying he was not campaigning and that Abia residents should re-elect him only if they considered his performance satisfactory. However, the governor, through his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, on Friday, dismissed the statement and the X account that published it as fake. Ekeoma, who signed the disclaimer, said Otti never made the statement and urged the public not to be misled by the publication. He explained that, contrary to the impression created by the viral post, the governor was already campaigning and had been touring different parts of the state to interact with voters and obtain firsthand feedback, particularly from grassroots communities. According to him, Otti considers campaigns a legitimate component of the electoral process and could not have disparaged politicians for engaging in them. “The Governor believes that campaigns are legitimate parts of the electoral process and thus could not have dismissed it or cast aspersions on those campaigning,” Ekeoma said. The state government urged members of the public to disregard the purported statement and the account responsible for circulating it, while calling on those behind the publication to immediately take it down and desist from misrepresenting the governor. It also cautioned individuals using Otti’s popularity to generate online traffic to ensure that information published in his name is truthful, warning that deliberate misrepresentation could attract the attention of law enforcement agencies. The disclaimer comes amid growing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, with social media increasingly serving as a platform for political messaging, claims and counterclaims. Meanwhile, Vanguard investigations indicate that Otti currently faces no formidable challenger in the forthcoming governorship election. item.title: 2027: Who speaks for the North as ACF crisis deepens?
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo As the 2027 general elections draw closer, an increasingly important question is emerging in Northern Nigeria: Who speaks for the North, and whose position represents the collective interests of the region? The question has assumed greater significance amid the lingering leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), one of the North’s longstanding socio-political platforms, and growing disagreements among prominent Northern politicians, elder statesmen and interest groups over the direction the region should take in the next general elections. For decades, the ACF provided an important platform for articulating Northern interests, engaging governments and promoting regional cohesion. However, its current internal disagreements, involving its Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, have raised questions about its ability to provide the kind of unified regional leadership expected of it at a critical political moment. The dispute has reportedly degenerated into competing claims of authority, allegations of constitutional breaches and disagreements over the management of the organisation’s affairs. The development may create an opening for other political and socio-cultural platforms to occupy the space traditionally associated with the ACF. However, its current internal disagreements, involving its Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, have raised questions about its ability to provide the kind of unified regional leadership expected of it at a critical political moment. The dispute has reportedly degenerated into competing claims of authority, allegations of constitutional breaches and disagreements over the management of the organisation’s affairs. The development may create an opening for other political and socio-cultural platforms to occupy the space traditionally associated with the ACF. Indeed, the struggle over who represents Northern opinion became more apparent on Wednesday when the Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table challenged some prominent Northern figures over their criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. At a press conference in Kaduna, the group, through its chairman, Abubakar A. Kurawa, faulted Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, Dr Usman Bugaje, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri and former National Health Insurance Scheme Executive Secretary, Prof Usman Yusuf, for what it described as presenting partisan political positions as the collective position of Northern Nigeria. In a briefing titled, Stop Hiding Naked Partisanship Behind the Sacred Robes of Arewa Eldership: You Do Not Speak for the North!, the organisation questioned the mandate under which the four personalities purportedly spoke for the region. It argued that neither previous public offices nor political prominence automatically conferred the authority to determine the political direction of the 19 Northern states. The group particularly questioned whether traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, professional associations, farmers, traders and ordinary citizens had been adequately consulted before positions were presented as representing the North. It also challenged the former public office holders to demonstrate their contributions to regional development, insisting that discussions about Northern leadership should go beyond political rhetoric to measurable achievements. Meanwhile, Murtala Mohammed, an Kaduna based critic, said the intervention has also brought another dimension to the debate: Whether those challenging the authority of established Northern voices are themselves speaking from a sufficiently broad regional mandate. “The argument is significant because the four personalities criticised by the group are entitled, like other Nigerians, to express their political opinions and question government policies”, he said. “The more important distinction is between expressing personal or partisan positions and claiming to represent an entire region.” Political realignments The controversy comes against the background of increasing political realignments ahead of 2027. While some Northern politicians and groups have expressed reservations about the Tinubu administration, others are advocating continuity and greater engagement with the Federal Government. At the Kaduna Summit on Inclusivity, Good Governance and Sustainable Development organised by the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation on Wednesday, former Niger State Governor, Mu’azu Babangida Aliyu, endorsed Governor Uba Sani for a second term, citing his administration’s record in security, education, healthcare, agriculture and infrastructure. The foundation’s Director-General, Abubakar Gambo Umar, also highlighted the importance of continuity and inclusive governance. Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented by Deputy Speaker Ado Doguwa, called for accountability and constructive criticism while acknowledging continuing security challenges, particularly in Southern Kaduna. Governor Uba Sani, however, went beyond the immediate Kaduna political debate, urging the foundation to mobilise Northern leaders towards developing a comprehensive regional development agenda. He recalled the vision of the late Premier of Northern Nigeria, Sir Ahmadu Bello, for a united, peaceful and self-sufficient North, arguing that subsequent generations of leaders had departed from that vision. His call raises an important question: Can Northern leaders agree on a common development agenda despite their differences over political parties, presidential succession and the 2027 elections? Platforms There are also other emerging platforms. The League of Northern Democrats, led by former Kano State Governor Ibrahim Shekarau, has been engaging the ACF, Northern Elders Forum and Middle Belt Forum on the possibility of building a common front around the region’s challenges. Yet, the existence of several organisations does not necessarily translate into a coherent regional voice. “The North’s problems extend beyond political representation. Insecurity, poverty, unemployment, educational backwardness, agricultural difficulties, infrastructure deficits and economic hardship require sustained engagement and measurable interventions,” said Murtala. “Consequently, the question of who speaks for the North should not be reduced to who supports or opposes Tinubu, who wants power returned to the region or which political camp commands the loudest following. “Neither should the North be treated as a politically homogeneous constituency whose millions of people must necessarily subscribe to one political position”. The ACF crisis therefore presents an opportunity for serious introspection. Its founding mission of promoting Northern unity and socio-economic advancement remains relevant, but rebuilding confidence in the organisation requires resolving its internal disagreements and restoring its institutional credibility. Similarly, emerging Arewa groups must demonstrate inclusiveness, independence and accountability rather than simply becoming competing platforms for political interests. Ultimately, Northern leadership ahead of 2027 should be measured not by the ability to mobilise endorsements, issue press statements or condemn political opponents, but by the capacity to develop a common agenda, build consensus across regional divides and hold governments accountable. He said such differences did not detract from the forum’s commitment to consultation, constructive engagement and advocacy on issues of common interest, including good governance in all its ramifications. He explained that the ACF remained committed to holding elected officials accountable, promoting the fight against corruption and advocating policies that would advance the welfare of the people. Baba noted that the forum had consistently called on governments at all levels to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity, stressing that it had never relented in demanding decisive action against the persistent security challenges confronting the North. item.description: By Nnamdi Ojiego Honourable Babatunde Oduyoye was the Chief Whip of the Alliance for Democracy in the House of Representatives where he represented Ibadan Nort-West /South-West Federal Constituency between 1999 and 2007. He had also served as Special Adviser on Political Matters to Governor Seyi Makinde, as well as a member of Oyo State Advisory Council. He is one of the appointees that opened the recent gale of resignations from the government of Oyo State. In this interview, he speaks on why he left Makinde, why he is teaming up with other progressives to support the reelection of President Bola Tinubu and why the progressives need to undertake a rescue mission in Oyo State. Excerpts: Some time ago, you announced your resignation from Oyo State Advisory Council, thus opening the floodgates for the resignations of many others from Governor Seyi Makinde’s government. After the announcement, we didn’t hear much from you. What happened? The Advisory Council is expected to advise the governor on the policy, politics, and administration. As of the time I resigned, I mentioned personal reasons, and it was to improve myself in certain areas. Apart from that, I had a feeling that the council had outlived its usefulness. Once you have a council that is not up and doing, or is doing the proper thing, and the governor is not recognising it, there was no need to sit in that council anymore. That is why, honorably, I resigned. In the resignation letter, you said you had not joined any other party apart from the Alliance for Democracy (AD). And we know that the AD is no longer a registered political party. Can you give us an insight into your political direction going forward? I was, at no point in time, a card-carrying member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), neither did I attend any local government or state meeting. But there was never a time they called a meeting of leaders of the PDP in the southwestern part that they invited me. The circumstances surrounding the breakdown of that marriage have not been publicly established. During the introduction of his new wife, Jimmy said his first marriage had ended before he became senior pastor in September 2023. The trustees, however, described the remarriage and its public blessing as contrary to the church’s teachings, the values of its founders and the standards expected of its spiritual leadership. They said the development had caused distress among members and brought the church into public controversy and disrepute. Their statement placed the marriage alongside the disagreement over the succession recording as grounds for their action against him. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. Jimmy and the church’s opposing leadership position rejected the announcement, insisting that his appointment in September 2023 was unanimously approved by the Board of Trustees and that those who announced his removal lacked the constitutional authority to do so. The disagreement escalated when the Lagos State High Court, on Wednesday issued an interim order restraining Jimmy from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head, and from interfering with its governance and activities. The order was made ex parte while the case was adjourned until December 1. Sealed Meanwhile, the church, on Friday, dismissed reports that its premises had been sealed and announced that its regular Sunday service would hold at 9am, although its 2026 Thanksgiving Service had been postponed. At the centre of the dispute are questions that extend beyond the personalities involved. How should a church founded and led by one individual determine who succeeds that person? Does a founder’s recorded preference override a later appointment made under the church’s constitution? What role should family members, trustees, elders and other senior ministers play? And how can a ministry preserve its identity while ensuring that leadership is transferred through a process accepted by its members? For churches whose growth, public identity and authority have been closely associated with their founders, succession can involve spiritual, administrative, legal and family considerations. Pattern The experiences of other Nigerian churches show that there is no single pattern. The Church of God Mission International, founded by Archbishop Benson Idahosa, offers an example of a founder’s widow taking over leadership. Following his death in March 1998, his wife, Margaret Idahosa, succeeded him as presiding bishop. She had been actively involved in the ministry before his death. Their son, Bishop Faith Benson Idahosa, has also held leadership positions within the church’s institutions. The transition at the Synagogue Church of All Nations (SCOAN) also brought a founder’s widow to the forefront. After the death of Prophet T.B. Joshua in June 2021, his wife, Evelyn Joshua, emerged as the church’s leader. The transition attracted public attention amid reports of disagreements over the church’s future. The church denied that there was a succession battle and said it would follow its founder’s instructions. In September 2021, the Federal High Court in Lagos affirmed Evelyn Joshua as a trustee of SCOAN after a petition to fill the vacancy created by her husband’s death. A similar family transition occurred at New Anointing Ministries in Makurdi, founded by the late Rev. Godwin Ikyernum. Following his death in an automobile accident in March 1997, his wife, Hannah Ikyernum, assumed leadership. The ministry is now led by their son, Pastor Joshua Ikyernum. Accounts of the transition have also documented dissatisfaction among some of the founder’s former associates, with some reportedly leaving the ministry. Succession without spouses, children as beneficiaries Other churches have followed succession arrangements that did not depend on a founder’s spouse or children. The leadership of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), founded by the late Rev. Josiah Akindayomi, passed to Pastor Enoch Adeboye in 1981. The church’s account of the transition says Akindayomi communicated his choice of successor in a sealed pronouncement that was read after his burial. Adeboye, who was not the founder’s biological son, subsequently became General Overseer. At the Foursquare Gospel Church in Nigeria, leadership has also changed through an electoral process. In July 2019, delegates elected Rev. Sam Aboyeji as the church’s fifth General Overseer, succeeding Rev. Felix Meduoye, who had completed an eight-year tenure. Aboyeji emerged through a contest involving other candidates, including Rev. Isaac Komolafe. The Upper Room Baptist Church provides another example of an institutionally managed transition. The church, which began in 1987 with 17 founding families, operates a governance structure involving a General Council, Trustees and a General Assembly. Pastor Oluleke Akinola succeeded its first General Overseer, Pastor Abiodun Longe, in 2004. After 21 years in office, Akinola handed over to Pastor Rufus Dada on December 31, 2024. The Apostolic Church Nigeria also experienced a leadership transition through an election in February 2025, when Pastor Lawrence Oladele emerged as National Leader. These examples illustrate the range of arrangements available to churches: Succession by a spouse or child, appointment of a designated successor, election by delegates and leadership transitions managed through established institutional structures. item.title: ABBACARE: How Kano is expanding healthcare access for the most vulnerable
item.description: By Hassan A. Karofi Access to affordable healthcare remains a major challenge for millions of Nigerians, particularly low-income households and vulnerable groups who often delay or forgo treatment because of the cost. In Kano State, the ABBACARE Initiative is one of the interventions aimed at addressing this challenge through social health insurance. Implemented by the Kano State Contributory Healthcare Management Agency (KSCHMA), ABBACARE is designed to provide healthcare coverage for vulnerable groups, including pregnant women, persons living with sickle cell disorder and emergency patients. Its focus is on reducing the financial barriers that prevent people from accessing essential medical services. According to figures provided for the initiative, ABBACARE has enrolled 28,721 beneficiaries and extended service delivery to 13 hospitals across Kano State’s three senatorial zones. These figures point to an effort to widen access to healthcare, although the programme’s long-term impact will depend on the quality of services available, the regularity of funding and the ability to sustain coverage as more people are enrolled. The initiative also highlights the role state governments can play in advancing Universal Health Coverage through social health insurance. While national policies provide an important framework, state-level programmes such as ABBACARE can help address local healthcare needs and extend financial protection to people who might otherwise struggle to pay for treatment. The programme is part of a wider set of health interventions under Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s administration. Another is the Gida-Gida Lafiya Project, which focuses on hypertension and other non-communicable diseases through the distribution of customised digital blood pressure monitors. The devices are intended to help beneficiaries monitor their blood pressure, identify possible health risks early and seek medical attention when necessary. Their adaptation to provide guidance in local languages also reflects the importance of making health information accessible to people in their communities. Although ABBACARE and Gida-Gida Lafiya address different aspects of healthcare, they speak to two related challenges. The former seeks to reduce the financial burden of accessing treatment, while the latter encourages prevention, regular monitoring and early intervention. Both approaches are relevant in a health system where the cost of treatment and late presentation at hospitals can worsen health outcomes. The question is whether the industry can deliver the volume of housing, infrastructure and commercial development required without fundamentally changing how it operates. That is where technology founders should pay attention. Construction is not just an engineering industry. It is a technology ecosystem waiting to be connected. One of the biggest misconceptions about construction technology is that innovation is primarily about drones, robotics, 3D printing or sophisticated building design software. Those technologies matter, but they represent only a fraction of the opportunity. Construction is also an industry of financial transactions, procurement networks, logistics, labour coordination, data management, risk assessment, asset management and complex workflows. Every construction project creates multiple interconnected problems that technology can solve. Consider what happens when someone decides to build a house. They need to verify land ownership, develop architectural and structural drawings, estimate project costs, secure financing, identify qualified professionals, procure materials, engage artisans, manage construction activities, monitor expenditure and verify completion. Each stage involves multiple stakeholders, financial commitments and operational decisions. In many African markets, these activities are still managed through disconnected systems. There is an opportunity to build technology infrastructure that connects this entire process. Opportunities that could redefine construction in Africa AI-powered construction cost intelligence: One of the most persistent problems in construction is inaccurate project costing. Material prices fluctuate. Labour rates differ by location. Transportation costs change. Exchange-rate movements affect imported materials, while poor historical data makes reliable forecasting difficult. An intelligent construction cost engine could combine material prices, labour rates, geographical information, historical project costs and market conditions to generate more reliable estimates. Imagine a developer being able to estimate the cost of constructing a residential building in Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan or Accra using current market information rather than relying entirely on outdated rate books. Buyers frequently depend on personal contacts, multiple quotations and informal supplier relationships. Beyond convenience, such a platform could improve price discovery, reduce procurement fraud and create a more accountable supply chain. Traditional construction financing is often inaccessible, while informal savings arrangements do not necessarily provide the structure or safeguards required for long-term building projects. For example, a customer could save towards land documentation, architectural design, foundation construction, roofing and finishing. This creates an opportunity to connect personal finance, construction delivery and financial inclusion. item.title: Anambra’s Ekwulobia flyover to be commissioned November 27
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Executive Council has fixed November 27, 2026, for the formal commissioning and opening of the Ekwulobia flyover constructed by the administration of Governor Chukwuma Soludo. The flyover is strategically located at a junction that previously experienced serious traffic challenges, particularly during festive periods when vehicular movement increases significantly. Rising from its meeting in Awka, the State Executive Council directed that all necessary arrangements be made to ensure a successful and hitch-free commissioning. However, it did not disclose who would perform the ceremony. The state Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, described the flyover as one of the flagship urban regeneration projects of the Soludo administration. He said the project stood alongside the transformation of Okpoko, formerly regarded as the biggest urban slum in the South-East, into an area characterised by improved infrastructure, order and human dignity. “These projects underscore Governor Soludo’s irreversible commitment to building a liveable, prosperous and smart mega-city in Anambra State,” Mefor said. Meanwhile, the Council resolved to move the state’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) drive from moral suasion to full enforcement, including the prosecution of tax evaders, to maximise the state’s revenue potential. It consequently urged residents, business owners and other taxpayers to pay their taxes and levies promptly to avoid the consequences of enforcement, particularly prosecution. According to the Council, no modern state can be built on voluntary compliance alone, stressing that payment of taxes is a civic responsibility. “Anambra will enforce it fairly and firmly,” the Council said. The Council also disclosed that it had concluded work on the state’s 2027 budget, which Governor Soludo is expected to present to the Anambra State House of Assembly on Tuesday. Mefor described the proposed budget as a consolidation budget designed to deepen the gains of Solution 2.0 in infrastructure, security, education, healthcare, youth empowerment and economic transformation. item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. This is an important lesson in China’s approach to infrastructure: transportation infrastructure is being connected to manufacturing, commerce and international trade. What does this mean for Africa? At first glance, one might wonder how a railway connecting China to Europe has any direct relevance to Africa. After all, China and Africa are separated by thousands of kilometres of land and sea, and maritime shipping remains the principal channel for trade between them. But the relevance of the China-Europe Railway Express to Africa is not necessarily that African countries should be connected to the same railway. It is the broader economic thinking behind it. China’s approach demonstrates the value of integrating transportation, logistics, industrial development and international markets. Africa needs to pay attention to this model. For African countries, better connectivity could transform the movement of goods within the continent, improve access to international markets and strengthen regional trade. Imagine agricultural produce from northern Nigeria moving efficiently by rail to processing centres, industrial zones and seaports for export. Imagine manufacturers in Kano, Kaduna, Aba and other commercial centres having reliable connections to ports and distribution networks, reducing the cost and time involved in moving their products. item.title: Chelsea Humbled As Leeds Run Riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to West London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Leeds United’s English goalkeeper #01 James Trafford and Leeds United’s Swiss striker #19 Noah Okafor celebrate after the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in London on November 21, 2026. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP) Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks, and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. item.content:encoded: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to West London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Leeds United’s English goalkeeper #01 James Trafford and Leeds United’s Swiss striker #19 Noah Okafor celebrate after the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in London on November 21, 2026. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP) Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks, and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.
